title: Makan sini ke bungkus?
blurb: Eating in or taking away — bungkus, tapau and the drink in a bag.

notes.title: … ke …?
notes.body: ke between two choices means “or?” — standard Malay would use atau. Makan sini ke bungkus? is the first thing you'll hear at many counters.

notes.title: bungkus and tapau
notes.body: Both mean takeaway. Bungkus (to wrap) is Malay; tapau comes from Cantonese and is just as common in KL.

notes.title: ikat tepi
notes.body: A takeaway drink in a plastic bag tied at the side with a straw poking out. Say ikat tepi and you'll get exactly that.

p4.en: One iced milk tea, in a tied bag.
p4.note: ikat tepi = tied at the side; the classic takeaway drink bag.

p5.en: It's a ten-minute wait, is that okay?

p10.en: Gravies separate, please — don't mix them.

p12.en: Call me when it's ready, okay.

p13.en: Want to wait or come back?

dialogue.en: Eating here or takeaway?
Takeaway.
What would you like?

dialogue.ms: Nasi goreng satu, teh ais satu.
dialogue.en: One fried rice, one iced milk tea.
Okay, wait a moment.
Okay, thank you.

gist.q: Is she eating in or taking away?
options: Taking away fried rice and an iced tea
Eating in with fried rice and an iced tea
Taking away only a drink
Eating here or takeaway?
Do you want to eat or drink?
Are you eating alone?
Okay, wait a moment.
Okay, it's ready.
Okay, sit here.
Bungkus.
Terima kasih.
Tunggu kejap ye.
exercises.why: It's an either/or question — pick one: “Makan sini” or “Bungkus”.

dialogue.en: Eating here or takeaway?

dialogue.ms: Bungkus. Nasi goreng kampung satu, mee goreng satu.
dialogue.en: Takeaway. One kampung fried rice, one fried noodles.
Both to take away?

dialogue.ms: Ha'ah, dua-dua. Mee goreng tu tak nak pedas.
dialogue.en: Yep, both. The fried noodles not spicy.
Drinks?
One iced milk tea, in a tied bag.

dialogue.ms: Okay. Kena tunggu sepuluh minit, boleh?
dialogue.en: Okay. It's a ten-minute wait, is that alright?
Sure, no problem. I'll wait here.

gist.q: What will she do while the food is prepared?
options: Wait there for about ten minutes
Come back in an hour
Sit down and eat in instead
Cancel the drink
gist.why: Kena tunggu sepuluh minit … saya tunggu sini.

options: Yes, both. The fried noodles not spicy.
Yes, both. The fried rice extra spicy.
No, just one. The noodles are for here.
It's a ten-minute wait, is that alright?
It'll be ready in two minutes.
You have to pay ten ringgit first, okay?
Boleh, takpe. Saya tunggu sini.
Dua-dua bungkus?
Teh ais satu, ikat tepi.
exercises.why: He's checking you're okay to wait; “Boleh, takpe” says it's no problem.

dialogue.en: Can I get takeaway?
Sure, sure. What do you want to take away?

dialogue.ms: Nasi goreng kampung dua. Satu pedas, satu tak nak pedas langsung, untuk budak.
dialogue.en: Two kampung fried rice. One spicy, one not spicy at all, for a kid.

dialogue.ms: Okay. Yang tak pedas tu nak letak telur mata?
dialogue.en: Okay. Want a fried egg on the non-spicy one?

dialogue.ms: Boleh jugak. Lepas tu roti canai tiga, kuah asing-asing ye, jangan campur.
dialogue.en: Sure. And then three roti canai, gravies separate, please — don't mix them.
Dhal or curry?

dialogue.ms: Dhal dua, kari satu. Eh, air pun nak. Teh o ais dua, ikat tepi.
dialogue.en: Two dhal, one curry. Oh, drinks too. Two iced teas without milk, in tied bags.

dialogue.ms: Ikat tepi dua. Sudu garpu nak?
dialogue.en: Two in tied bags. Do you want spoons and forks?

dialogue.ms: Tak payah lah, makan kat rumah je.
dialogue.en: No need, we're just eating at home.

dialogue.ms: Okay. Ramai orang sikit ni, dalam lima belas minit siap. Nak tunggu ke datang balik?
dialogue.en: Okay. It's a bit busy now, ready in about fifteen minutes. Want to wait or come back?

dialogue.ms: Saya tunggu lah. Dah siap panggil ye.
dialogue.en: I'll wait. Call me when it's ready, okay.

gist.q: Which detail is right about this takeaway order?
options: One fried rice is not spicy at all, for a child
She wants the gravies mixed together
She asked for extra spoons and forks
She will come back in fifteen minutes
gist.why: Satu tak nak pedas langsung, untuk budak.

options: Two fried rice: one spicy, one not spicy at all, for a kid.
Two fried rice, both very spicy.
One fried rice for a kid, not spicy.
Two fried rice: one for here, one takeaway.
It's a bit busy; about fifteen minutes. Wait or come back?
It's quiet; five minutes. Please sit down.
We're closing in fifteen minutes; come back tomorrow.
Fifteen people are waiting; better come back later.
Tak payah lah, makan kat rumah je.
Dah siap panggil ye.
Kuah dhal ke kari?
exercises.why: He's offering cutlery; “Tak payah” politely turns it down.
